title: Gritters: when & where
excerpt: Rochdale's seven gritters are back out on main roads, bus routes and school streets. Here is when they grit, which roads they cover and where to find a grit bin.
body:
Rochdale Borough Council's gritters are back out across the borough, from Middleton to Littleborough, treating main roads, bus routes and school streets as temperatures fall again.

Councillor Dylan Williams, the council's cabinet member for highways and facilities, said the highways team had already carried out its first full grit of the winter.

Councillor Williams spent an afternoon at the depot with Gavin, one of the service's supervisors, inspecting the fleet of seven gritters and the grit stockpile for this winter.

He said: "We are well prepared. The team conducted the first full grit last night."

When the gritters go out

The council says it usually grits in the evening from about 6.30pm, or in the morning at about 4.30am, when the grit works best.

It avoids rush hours because gritters get stuck in traffic, and sometimes waits for rain to stop so the grit is not washed away.

Councillor Williams said the decision to send the gritters out is based on weather stations in Middleton, Norden and Littleborough, and computers that monitor road temperatures.

Cameras also watch several roads around the clock, including Hollin Lane and Blackstone Edge.

"The vehicles are also tracked on a live map so we can see that all of the roads are done and at what times," he said.

"Our team of gritter drivers are out 24/7, including overnight in the early hours of the morning working very hard to keep our Borough moving."

Where they grit

The council has seven planned gritting routes covering roughly 208 miles of road, and each route takes around four hours to complete.

There are around 450 miles of road in the borough, and the council says it cannot afford to grit them all.

Lists of the roads on each route are published on the council's gritting pages at rochdale.gov.uk.

The council asks drivers to avoid double parking at gritting times, as some roads, including Norton Rose and Barn Meadows, are hard for the gritters to get through.

Grit bins

There are more than 700 grit bins on residential streets across the borough, and Councillor Williams said all of them have been restocked for the cold weather.

He said the borough has the largest stock of residential grit bins in Greater Manchester.

The council says anyone can use the salt in the bins on public roads and pavements, including roads that are not on a gritting route.

What comes next

The council plans to release a video next week showing more of how the roads are kept clear.

Gritting updates are posted under #RochdaleGrit on X, and the council's Highways and Engineering Service can be contacted on 0300 303 8879.

Source: Statement from Councillor Dylan Williams, Rochdale Borough Council cabinet member for highways and facilities, supplied to Rochdale Daily; Rochdale Borough Council gritting and winter service pages. Photograph: Councillor Dylan Williams / supplied.
